citation: Conley, Walter H. (copyright holder) and O. E. Stelzer (artist), with Caroline M. McIlvaine (historical adviser). A map of Chicago: incorporated as a town August 5, 1833. 1933.
author: Walter H. Conley and O. E. Stelzer
repository: Norman B. Leventhal Map & Education Center, Boston Public Library
locator: identifier 06_01_014768; 44 x 64 cm, scale approx. 1:5,450, oriented north to the right
note: A 1933 RECONSTRUCTION, not a period document — pictorial elevations of individual 1833 structures with modern street names. The single richest building-level inventory available. Conley spent about two years in libraries and archives; Caroline McIlvaine had thirty years earlier collected data directly from the last surviving pioneers, so this is a real evidentiary chain with one weak link rather than a decoration. USE (revised 2026-08-10, at Kevin's direction): asset_use 'orientation' — it may carry a position, a street relationship or the existence of a structure to INFERRED, with a note naming it. It may never reach 'documented', and no outline, footprint or shoreline is traced from it: a pictorial elevation tells you a thing was there, not what shape it was. It demonstrably errs — it labels the du Sable/Kinzie house 'built 1832' against every documentary source (see data/exclusions.json) — which is the reason for that ceiling. Previously tagged 'cross_check', which left things conjectural that this map actually attests, i.e. claimed no evidence existed when some did. rights_status stays check_required: cite it freely, derive no ASSET from it.
rights_note: BPL asserts 'no known copyright restrictions', but a dealer reports the Library of Congress copy stamped (c) CIF 5380, Mar-7 1933. A 1933 US publication is public domain only if the 1961 renewal lapsed. Run a Stanford Copyright Renewal Database check and record the outcome here before deriving any asset.
